patch.objective: Know how delegation works for the PN: the delegating nurse stays accountable, nursing judgment cannot be delegated, and state law decides whether an LPN/VN may delegate to assistive personnel
secondaryObjectives: Tell assignment from delegation: assignment covers routine care within someone's scope or basic training, delegation hands over a specific task beyond their usual role after competence is checked

sources.note: Relayed from the LPN/VN course's earlier cases (read 2026-11-11, primary PDF), not re-read for this band: the practical nursing course is built toward this test plan.
The objective and secondary objectives are the course's own titles.

Relayed from the NCLEX-PN case aide-feeding-thin-liquids-dysphagia, not re-read for this band; its note: Relayed from the REQ-233 NCLEX-PN cases (read 2026-11-11, primary PDF), not re-read: Coordinated Care includes care within the legal scope of practice; Physiological Adaptation includes recognizing and reporting a change in the client's condition.

sources.cite: ANA and NCSBN. National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation (joint statement, effective 2019-04-01)
sources.note: Relayed from the NCLEX-PN case aide-feeding-thin-liquids-dysphagia, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch with quotes of the PDF: 'The licensed nurse who delegates the "responsibility" maintains overall accountability for the patient'; 'the delegatee bears the responsibility for the delegated activity'; 'The licensed nurse should be ready and available to intervene as necessary'; the delegatee must tell the licensed nurse when the patient's condition changes; 'The licensed nurse cannot delegate nursing judgment'; LPN/VNs delegate only as allowed by their state or jurisdiction; the five rights: right task, circumstance, person, directions and communication, supervision and evaluation.

sources.cite: American Stroke Association. Trouble Swallowing After Stroke (Dysphagia) (stroke.org, undated; describes swallowing after ASHA)
sources.note: Relayed from the NCLEX-PN case aide-feeding-thin-liquids-dysphagia, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch with quotes: warning signs include 'coughing during or right after eating or drinking' and 'having a wet or gurgly voice during or after eating or drinking'; aspiration can be silent; unmanaged dysphagia 'can lead to poor nutrition, pneumonia and disability'; a speech-language pathologist evaluates swallowing; liquids are thinned or thickened as advised; 'Sit up straight when you eat or drink'.
